paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Before the Levites did one day of work at the Tent of Meeting, the LORD had them cleansed, and atonement was made for them (Numbers 8:6; Numbers 8:12; Numbers 8:21). Nobody got to serve on talent alone. The LORD says all of it will separate them, and then He says the Levites "will belong to Me" (Numbers 8:14). The belonging came first, and the work came after.

Now look at WHY they were taken. The LORD says every firstborn in Israel is His, set apart on the day He struck down the firstborn in Egypt, and He took the Levites "in place of all the firstborn" (Numbers 8:17; Numbers 8:18). So their service wasn't a side job, baker. It was a gift to Aaron and his sons, and it was for the Israelites, so that no plague would come against them when they approached the sanctuary (Numbers 8:19).

And I love how the LORD plans the whole stretch of a Levite's service, right down to the later years. At fifty a man retires from the work, but he may still assist his brothers (Numbers 8:25; Numbers 8:26). I think that shows the LORD cares about the man and not only the work. Nobody got shoved to the back of a drawer at fifty, and I would KNOW about that.
